root_cause.text: The bridge CFM subsystem uses `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` to stop the `ccm_rx_dwork` delayed work before freeing a peer MEP structure, but this function only cancels pending work without preventing new scheduling; `br_cfm_frame_rx()` running concurrently in softirq context under RCU read lock can re-schedule the work via `ccm_rx_timer_start()` between the cancellation and the `kfree_rcu()` call, causing use-after-free when the rescheduled work executes on the freed memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` with `disable_delayed_work_sync()` in peer MEP deletion paths. The CVE description explicitly shows the race window: after `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` returns (line 1), `br_cfm_frame_rx()` on cpu1 can still call `ccm_rx_timer_start()` which queues the work (line 2), and then `kfree_rcu()` frees the peer_mep structure (line 3), leaving the queued work to execute on freed memory. The `disable_delayed_work_sync()` function prevents this by disabling the work queue itself, rejecting any subsequent `queue_delayed_work()` calls, whereas `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` only cancels currently pending work.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace cancel_delayed_work_sync with disable_delayed_work_sync to prevent use-after-free when peer MEP structures are freed during cleanup.
intent_record.what: Changed function call from `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` to `disable_delayed_work_sync()` when cleaning up peer MEP list entries during MEP deletion.
intent_record.how: This changes the delayed work cancellation behavior. `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` cancels and waits for any pending work to complete, while `disable_delayed_work_sync()` disables the work queue and waits for in-flight executions to finish without canceling queued work. This prevents the delayed work from being re-queued after the peer_mep structure is freed via kfree_rcu().

intent_record.intent_summary: Inline the peer MEP disable operation to directly synchronize delayed work cancellation before freeing the peer MEP structure.
intent_record.what: Replaced a call to `cc_peer_disable(peer_mep)` with a direct call to `disable_delayed_work_sync(&peer_mep->ccm_rx_dwork)`.
intent_record.how: This change makes the delayed work cancellation explicit and synchronous at the point of peer MEP removal. Instead of delegating to a wrapper function, the code now directly synchronizes the cancellation of the CCM RX delayed work, ensuring the work is fully stopped before the peer_mep structure is freed via kfree_rcu.

Specifically: (1) The `br_cfm_frame_rx()` function (lines 369-465) runs under RCU read lock and can call `ccm_rx_timer_start(peer_mep)` at line 421 to reschedule the `ccm_rx_dwork` delayed work. (2) The `cc_peer_disable()` function (lines 147-150) uses `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&peer_mep->ccm_rx_dwork)` to stop the work. (3) In `mep_delete_implementation()` (lines 558-575), line 560 calls `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&peer_mep->ccm_rx_dwork)` followed by `kfree_rcu(peer_mep, rcu)` at line 561. (4) The vulnerability exists because `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` only cancels pending work but does not prevent new scheduling. Since `br_cfm_frame_rx()` runs in softirq context under RCU read lock, it can execute concurrently and reschedule the work via `ccm_rx_timer_start()` between the `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` call and the `kfree_rcu()` call, causing use-after-free when the rescheduled work executes on freed memory. The code lacks synchronization to prevent this race condition.

According to the vulnerability description, `br_cfm_frame_rx()` running concurrently in softirq context can re-schedule work via `ccm_rx_timer_start()` between any cancellation attempt and the `kfree_rcu()` call. The code directly frees peer_mep structures without preventing concurrent work scheduling, creating a use-after-free vulnerability when rescheduled work executes on freed memory.
